AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine’s nomination of Roland Kedikian for GWP Commission will be
  placed on the City Council Agenda for March 7th. Devine announced that SoCal Gas has
  new programs to assist customers over 55 years old and who are struggling financially with
  their gas bills, using charitable donations of $10 million dollars ($5M will be used for gas
  assistance fund and administered by United Way, $4M will be used to relaunch the fuel and
  communities program to help relieve food insecurity by collaborating with local food banks,
  and $1M will be used to fund the Restaurant Care Resilience Fund, intended for small
  restaurant owners to help with improvements in their property, employee retention and to
  manage debt, losses, and rising costs). More information can be found on SoCal’s website
  at www.socalgas.com/managehigherbills.

  Councilmember Asatryan announced it is International Woman’s Day on March 8, 2023, and
  a couple of events will take place that day. The Greater Downtown Glendale Association will
  be hosting an event at the MYA Rooftop from 2-5pm, tickets are available for purchase
  at www.downtownglendale.com. The Armenian Film Society is hosting a panel discussion
  on Armenian Women on Film and Entertainment at the Hero House @HyeRise at 7pm,
  tickets are available for purchase at https://www.herohouse.io/. Asatryan announced it is
  Employee Appreciation Day on March 3, 2023 and expressed her deepest gratitude to all
  city employees for doing their part, whether working remotely or here at City Hall.

  Councilmember Brotman echoed Asatryan’s comments regarding city employees. He
  nominated Daniel Paul to the Historic Preservation Commission (HPC). Brotman thanked
  Lorna Vartanian for her many years of service since she will be stepping down from the HPC
  after serving three terms. He asked staff to provide a report to reconsider how the city is
  defining major transit stop for the purposes of Assembly Bill 2097 authored by
  Assemblymember Friedman. Asatryan seconded.

  City Manager Golanian announced that he received a letter from the California Department
  of Housing and Community Development that the City of Glendale’s adopted Housing
  Element is now in substantial compliance with the State Housing Element Law. He
  congratulated Council for the direction and adoption of the Housing Element back in

  2
   November 2022, as well as city staff from the Planning Division, especially Deputy Director
  Erik Krause, who spent many hours drafting and revising the housing element. He also
  thanked the city’s consultant Amanda Tropiano, principal with the De Novo Planning Group,
  for her expertise, professionalism, and tenacity for working together with a team of attorneys
  and for collaborating with the city’s Planning Division. Devine mentioned it is very rare these
  days that a city would receive this type of approval from the state. Golanian indicated a
  report came out yesterday that half of the municipalities in California are vulnerable and not
  close to having their Housing Element adopted.

  Golanian expressed his deepest gratitude and appreciation to the crews of Public Works,
  Glendale Water and Power, Community Services and Parks, and Police and Fire Public
  Safety Personnel who worked tirelessly to mitigate the impacts of the recent storm events.
  He stated that the City of Glendale was notified by LA DWP that two of their Rinaldi Air Way
  Lines were impacted: one of them experienced substantial damage due to the storm and
  had to bring the other one down to make emergency repairs. Since Glendale’s lines are
  between the two systems of LA PD’s grid, there was a great potential of a system failure,
  essentially cutting off the City’s electricity from this external power source. Golanian sent his
  gratitude and appreciation to the GWP crew for their quick action in keeping the lights on
  and trying to mitigate the storm’s impact that would have otherwise cut-off the power when
  LADWP’s lines were damaged.
